pages.title: A Quiet Crisis
pages.text: The Charter is not at war. The Charter is rarely at war. The Charter writes letters.$(br2)But for the last two audit cycles, the letters have been getting odd. Dockets filed without surveyor signatures. Wax of the wrong colour. An entire Brass Hall session — minutes never published.

Senior Foremen speak of it in low voices at the back of teas. The phrase that gets used is $(o)"a rogue administrator."$() Nobody names the administrator out loud. Nobody is sure if there is just the one.$(br2)What is sure: forged Charter letterhead has surfaced in three colonies. The Charter has not acknowledged it.

A senior Foreman is, by old Charter convention, $(l)deputised$() during a crisis. The brass clip on the office desk is not decorative.$(br2)Erik says the same thing he always says. $(o)"Keep the books clean. The Charter audits eventually. Even itself."$()
